answer: The cheapest real defence: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because karst only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, dawn is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any sparrow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
